summary: Computer engineer (M.S. Computer Engineering, RIT, 2026) who builds the firmware between the sensor and the model: register-level bare-metal C on Cortex-M, interrupt-driven motor and servo control, and the Linux services that tie microcontrollers to NVIDIA Jetson edge compute.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Engineered a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control, streaming 3-DoF accelerometer motion from a Raspberry Pi over I2C and Bluetooth into HID commands.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Architected a metal-surface inspection pipeline for microscopic crack analysis that combines custom image stitching, wavelet denoising and depth estimation.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots, with UART and I2C sensor communication and closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++ on the Arduino, driving five servos with contact-aware grasping from dual time-of-flight sensors on an I2C multiplexer: a camera range gate plus a gripper that closes at 25 mm.
Deployed the Jetson arm bridge as a systemd service (auto-restart with backoff, non-root isolation, environment-based config) on static-IP networking for reliable multi-device WebSocket registration.
Drove the system to 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5 s voice-to-pick by hardening it against false-positive detections, servo brown-out and stale-frame capture.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Engineered Cortex-M4 temperature-monitoring firmware in bare-metal embedded C, with timer-synchronized sensing and a real-time display and no HAL or RTOS layer.
Programmed every peripheral at the register level (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1): timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a hand-written I2C driver.
Fit the complete firmware in 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Built a real-time tracking turret: YOLOv8 on an NVIDIA Jetson detects and tracks targets and streams control commands over UART to STM32 firmware.
Wrote multi-servo PWM control driven by interrupt-driven UART command handling, with a manual user override.
Coordinated sensing, control and display tasks under FreeRTOS with mutex-protected shared memory, adding time-of-flight range sensing and a live OLED distance readout.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot — Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Built closed-loop heading correction for a four-wheel holonomic robot on Arduino Due, deriving heading from dual-axis quadrature-encoder odometry (2400 CPR) and feeding the angular error back into rotation PWM.
Implemented interrupt-driven quadrature decoding from first principles as a 4-bit A/B transition state machine, and drove four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM.
